answer: In an AI agent economy, sybil resistance arises through progressive stake bonding where each agent must lock increasing collateral as its influence grows. A new identity starts with minimal rights, but to issue high-value actions it must deposit value proportional to its claimed reputation. Attackers face exponential cost because fabricating many identities requires locking real resources across them all, while genuine agents compound their stake like a comet gathering mass from an ocean of interactions, eventually forming a pearl of trusted capital that is expensive to fake.
